{% raw %}
`less`: show text a screen at a time.

## Synopsis

<strong>less</strong> \[<strong>-R</strong>\] \[<em>file</em>\]

## Description

<strong>less</strong> shows <em>file</em> (or, with no file or with <strong>-</strong>, what comes on standard input) one screen at a time. It draws on the terminal's alternate screen, with the tty in raw mode, and reads its keys from <em>/dev/tty</em>, so the text can come down a pipe. The whole input is read before anything is shown.

Long lines wrap at the terminal's width; a tab goes to the next multiple of 8 columns, and other control characters show as <strong>^X</strong> (the escape that starts a terminal's sequences as <strong>^\[</strong>, unless <strong>-R</strong> lets them through). Rows past the end show as <strong>~</strong>. The last row is the prompt: the file's name on the first screen, <strong>(END)</strong> on the last, else <strong>:</strong>.

When standard output is not a terminal, <strong>less</strong> copies the text to it, as <strong>cat</strong>(1) does. With no file named and standard input a terminal, it says "Missing filename" and exits 1.

## Options

<strong>-R</strong>
: Lets color and style sequences (<strong>ESC\[</strong>...<strong>m</strong>) through to the terminal, taking no room on the screen; a style goes on across a line's wrap. Searches find the text, not its styles.

## Environment

<strong>LESS</strong>
: Options, before the command line's: one with <strong>R</strong> in it is <strong>-R</strong>. <strong>man</strong>(1) sets it to <strong>-R</strong> for its pager when it isn't set, as man-db does.

## Commands

<strong>q Q</strong>
: Quit.

<strong>Space f ^F ^V PageDown</strong>
: Forward one screen.

<strong>b ^B PageUp</strong>
: Back one screen.

<strong>Enter j e ^N Down</strong>
: Forward one line.

<strong>k y ^P Up</strong>
: Back one line.

<strong>d ^D</strong>
: Forward half a screen.

<strong>u ^U</strong>
: Back half a screen.

<strong>g \< Home</strong>
: Go to the start.

<strong>G \> End</strong>
: Go to the end.

<strong>/</strong><em>text</em>
: Go to the next line containing <em>text</em> (a plain string, not a pattern), typed at the prompt and ended by Enter. Backspace edits it; Escape, or Backspace on an empty line, cancels. An empty <em>text</em> repeats the last search.

<strong>n</strong>
: Repeat the last search forward.

<strong>N</strong>
: Repeat the last search backward.

<strong>^L r</strong>
: Draw the screen again.

Other keys are ignored. ^C ends <strong>less</strong>, restoring the screen and the tty, with status 130.

## Exit status

0 on success; 1 if the file cannot be opened or no input was given; 130 if ended by ^C.

## Notes

There are no options; a word starting with <strong>-</strong> other than <strong>-</strong> itself is taken as a file name. The terminal's size is read once, at start.

## See also

<strong>cat</strong>(1), <strong>head</strong>(1), <strong>tail</strong>(1), <strong>man</strong>(1)
